soundstage.definition: The perceived size and space of the sound field.
soundstage.traits: Width, depth, and height of the virtual room.
soundstage.experience: Makes music feel like an open live concert or an intimate small room.

imaging.definition: The precise placement of instruments and voices within the soundstage.
imaging.experience: Allows you to point your finger at where the singer or guitar stands.

detailRetrieval.definition: The ability to reveal micro-textures and subtle background sounds.
detailRetrieval.experience: Lets you hear a breath intake, finger slides on guitar strings, or distant drum echoes.

timbre.definition: The natural, realistic tone quality of instruments and human voices.
timbre.traits: Realism, body, and lack of artificial metallic or plastic ringing.
timbre.experience: Makes a violin sound like wood and strings rather than a digital tone.

tonalBalance.definition: The relative volume levels of the bass, midrange, and treble frequencies.
tonalBalance.traits: Neutrality, warmth, brightness, or bass-heavy response.
tonalBalance.experience: Ensures no single frequency range overwhelms the music unnaturally.

settings.title: Settings
settings.savedNote: Changes are saved immediately to your config file and applied across the app.
settings.webFetchBody: “Fetch specs” in the device form looks up the current brand + model on the web — the squig.link measurement index (no key needed) for the frequency-response data and price, and keyless DuckDuckGo search to find manufacturer pages for impedance, sensitivity, driver type and the product image. Fetches are best-effort: fields that cannot be determined are left blank, and nothing is saved until you apply it. No API key is required and no credentials are stored.
settings.aboutBody: Audio Vault {{version}} — a local-first collection manager for audio gear. All data stays on this machine in your XDG directories.
